Note::bools¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

std::span<const std::uint8_t> Note::bools() const

Borrow The Native Boolean Lanes¶

bools() exposes a Bool Note’s contiguous lanes as a read-only borrowed span. It is the low-level boundary for algorithms that need direct iteration, a data pointer, or interoperability with code accepting std::span. The operation does not allocate, copy, stringify, flatten the Note object, or change its shape metadata.

Each lane is a canonical byte: 0 means false and 1 means true. The element type is std::uint8_t, not C++ bool, so the storage is genuinely contiguous and addressable; it does not use the packed proxy representation associated with std::vector<bool>. Treat values as truth values rather than arbitrary bytes. The returned span is const and cannot mutate the Note.

Order And Shape¶

The span is always one-dimensional because it is a memory view. Lanes appear in row-major logical order, while the original rank and extents remain on the Note. Use sizes() or size(dim) beside the span when an external kernel also needs shape. A scalar produces one lane; a defined empty shape produces an empty span.

Lifetime And Ownership¶

The span does not own storage. Keep the source Note, or another Note sharing the same backing buffer, alive for every access through the span. Copying a Note is cheap and keeps the buffer alive; copying only the span does not. Use host when the receiving code needs an independent owning copy.

bools() requires a defined Bool Note. Text, Bytes, Int64, and Float64 Notes are rejected instead of being converted. Call is_bool when the dtype is not statically known.

Example 1: Iterate Native Truth Values¶

const auto flags = pluss::note::make(std::vector<bool>{true, false});
const auto lanes = flags.bools();

std::cout << '[';
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lanes.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << (lanes[i] ? "true" : "false");
std::cout << "] size=" << lanes.size() << '\n';

Output¶

[true, false] size=2

Example 2: A Matrix Is Exposed In Row-Major Order¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<bool>{true, false, false, true},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto lanes = grid.bools();

std::cout << '[';
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lanes.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << (lanes[i] ? "true" : "false");
std::cout << "] shape=[" << grid.size(0) << ", " << grid.size(1) << "]\n";

Output¶

[true, false, false, true] shape=[2, 2]

The span has four lanes; [2, 2] remains metadata on grid.

Example 3: Note Copies Share The Borrowed Buffer¶

const auto flags = pluss::note::make(std::vector<bool>{true, false});
const auto copy = flags;
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "shared=" << (flags.bools().data() == copy.bools().data()) << '\n';

Output¶

shared=true

Either Note keeps the buffer alive. A span alone does not.

Example 4: Defined Empty Storage Produces An Empty Span¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<bool>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{0, 3});
std::cout << "empty lanes=" << empty.bools().size()
          << " shape=[" << empty.size(0) << ", " << empty.size(1) << "]\n";

Output¶

empty lanes=0 shape=[0, 3]

Example 5: Wrong Dtype And Undefined Are Distinct Failures¶

for (const auto& value : {pluss::note::make("text"),
                          pluss::Note::undefined()}) {
  try {
    (void)value.bools();
  } catch (const pluss::Error& error) {
    const std::string message(error.what());
    std::cout << message.substr(0, message.find('\n')) << '\n';
  }
}

Output¶

Note storage does not contain Bool lanes
Note::bools() on undefined Note
